text:
kevin: follow-up on tenant overrides precedence. we need a clear contract: when a tenant supplies an override that conflicts with global routing policy (e.g., changes weight/cap/region preference), what wins? i propose: 1) overlay semantics by default (tenant keys override matching global keys), 2) global authors can mark keys as 'sealed' to forbid overrides, 3) add a numeric cap attribute on sealed keys so tenants can request but not exceed a bound. thoughts?
anya: +1 for sealed keys + cap. also prefer that sealing is opt-in for sensitive fields (capacity_limits, latency_sla). enforcement at apply-time makes sense: validator rejects delta that contains tenant override for sealed path.
jessie: overlay vs namespaced: overlay is simpler for runtime lookup but makes debugging harder (which source set the value?). namespaced keeps provenance explicit but doubles lookup logic. can we keep overlay but emit provenance metadata on every resolved policy (source:global|tenant, delta_id)?
miguel: runtime perf note: don't re-merge overlays on every request. pre-merge per-tenant on delta apply and pointer-swap the tenant-entry. memory cost: estimate ~2KB per-tenant merged policy. for 50k tenants that's ~100MB, ok. eviction: LRU with soft TTL and remerge on next request if evicted.
sam: ops perspective: sealed keys + caps are good. add audit logs for any rejected tenant delta and metric counters: override_rejects_total, sealed_attempts_total. also when we pointer-swap merged tenant entry emit event with (tenant_id, new_version, prev_sig).
kevin: agree on provenance metadata + audit. api-level: GetPolicy(tenant_id) returns (policy_blob, provenance_map, policy_version). for sealed enforcement, validator should run both for global delta and tenant delta pipelines.
ops-bot: alert: validator rejected tenant override for tenant=acme-corp key=capacity_limits sealed=true delta=7954319999
jessie: migration question: existing global policies without explicit sealed flags should remain overridable. we should run a backfill that marks known sensitive keys as sealed after review, not auto-seal.
anya: CI lint: add rule that flags tenant delta introducing keys outside allowed schemas or exceeding cap. fail fast.
miguel: deterministic merge ordering: sort keys by stable path then apply overlay. ensure merge produces canonical JSON so we can compute a canonical hash/signature used for prev_sig checks. pseudocode:
```
merge(global, tenant) -> merged
  paths <- sorted(all_paths(global, tenant))
  for path in paths:
    if tenant.has(path) and not global[path].sealed:
      merged[path] = tenant[path]
      provenance[path] = "tenant"
    else:
      merged[path] = global[path]
      provenance[path] = "global"
  return canonicalize(merged), provenance
```
sam: also ensure ApplyDelta supports 'preview' mode that simulates merge for N tenants and returns diffs so we can run e2e tests before rollout.
kevin: action items: 1) add sealed+cap fields to policy schema + validator + CI lint (jessie + anya), 2) implement tenant pre-merge cache + pointer-swap + eviction policy (miguel), 3) telemetry/events for provenance and rejects + preview API (sam). i'll update RFC with schema examples and migration plan.
jessie: i'll draft the lint rules and a checklist for backfill.
kevin: cheers — schedule a 30m sync next Tue to review RFC updates if that works for everyone.
